title: What happens to the area as the top corner slides?
description: A base of six centimetres has a parallel line four centimetres above it, and a triangle stands on the base with its top corner on that line. The video finds the area from the base and the height, then slides the top corner and watches what stays and what changes. Keeko doubts that a leaning triangle with longer sides has more area.
teaching_notes: One idea: triangles on the same base with their top corner on a parallel line have the same height, so they have the same area. Watch for students who think longer sides mean more area.

source: BC = 6 cm and line l is parallel to BC, 4 cm away. Find the
video_script.why: The child sees that sliding the top corner along a parallel line keeps the height, so the area stays the same while the slanting sides and the perimeter change.
video_script.substitution: the book's base BC with a parallel line l above it; BC = 6 cm and the distance 4 cm
video_script.anchor: the book's base BC and the parallel line l, with several triangles on BC whose top corner A sits on l
video_script.wrong_answer: the leaning triangle has more area
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the triangle that leans furthest has more area because its slanting sides are longer. The area uses the base and the height, and the height has not changed.
video_script.payoff_line: The area is always twelve square centimetres
maths_rules: the line l is parallel to BC, so every point of l is 4 cm from BC; the height is 4 cm for every position of A
sliding A along l keeps the base 6 and the height 4, so the area stays 12 cm²
the slanting sides AB and AC change length as A moves, so the perimeter changes
check: A above the middle of BC gives AB = AC = 5, perimeter 16 cm; A above B gives AB = 4 and AC = √52 (about 7.21), perimeter about 17.21 cm; both areas are 12 cm²
video_script.design: One base and one parallel line all video. The top corner slides along the line, and the base and height are read at each place. Keeko's doubt: longer sides mean more area.
